about: Jesse Angelo is a photographer living in Aurora, Colorado. After roughly two decades in New York — much of it in Brooklyn — he now lives east of the city, where new development meets the open prairie of the High Plains.

He photographs slowly and returns often: a garden at the end of its season, an evening walk with a dog, the structures a demanding landscape is steadily wearing back to nothing. The work is made as books — sequenced bodies of work meant to be read in order, at a reader's pace.
It appeared that there was nothing there, but the more I slow down, the more I see.

cv.text: HOME: States of Belonging — Arvada Center Galleries, Arvada, CO ("Plains Skyscraper"), Jan 14 – Mar 28
Framed: Shadow and Light — Black Box Gallery, Portland, OR, On-Line Annex ("Lattice Silhouette")

books.title: None of This Belongs Here
books.description: The High Plains and the things built on it — the imposed one-mile grid, and the climate wearing it all back to nothing.

books.title: Evening Walks With Pancho
books.description: Evening walks in the neighborhood with a golden dog: fences, rooflines, dusk skies.

books.title: Fall of the Brooklyn Botanic Garden
books.description: A garden at the end of its season, photographed in late fall and first snow.
